entity.scope_notes: 800 m nearest-stop catchment around BTS Nana. District split (app data): Watthana 48%, Khlong Toei 44%, Pathum Wan 8%. NOT the Chinatown Soi Nana — that cocktail-bar strip sits in Pom Prap Sattru Phai inside st.wat-mangkon's catchment (batch-2 verified). Research-verified: Nana Plaza ~255–300 m inside; Bumrungrad campus straddles the NW boundary (frontage ~415–450 m inside, geotagged center ~710 m outside the polygon); Benchasiri ~1.7 km east and Lumphini ~1.6–1.7 km south both outside — green 10 is not reproducible from in-unit geometry (1.4 ha mapped, identity unresolved).

selection_context.popularity_method: No citywide popularity measure has been collected. Coverage breadth was measured for batch selection only (2024-11-05..2026-11-07 window, publisher-family dedup, coverage-scan.json); it is a research-selection signal, not a popularity score.
selection_context.selection_rationale: Popular-but-contested nightlife identity; the Soi Nana name confusion is a Q01 test; green 10 with 1.4 ha park is a green-geometry outlier.

claims.text_en: The 'Nana' name in this area derives from the Lek-Nana (เล็ก-นานา) family, a prominent Thai-Chinese merchant family whose landholding gave its name to Soi Nana and to BTS Nana station; Soi Nana is Sukhumvit Soi 4, paired across the road with Soi 3 (Nana Tai/Nana Nuea), and BTS Nana (E3) is the nearest stop.

temporal_scope.notes: Historical naming; 1958 shophouse conversion date given by ThaiHometown

evidence.paraphrase: Soi Nana takes its name from the Lek-Nana family; in 1958 (B.E. 2501) a family descendant converted family land into rental shophouses, land that included what became the Grace Hotel area
Nana Plaza's name comes from the property-holding Nana family, with Lek Nana the most prominent member

limitations: Chinese-origin derivation of the word Nana ('nine') is stated only by ThaiHometown and not corroborated

claims.text_en: Bangkok has two well-known 'Soi Nana' streets: the Sukhumvit Soi 4 one in this unit (nightlife/red-light area) and a separate bar-hopping Soi Nana in Chinatown (Talat Noi/Song Wat, off Rama IV near Hua Lamphong); Condé Nast Traveler explicitly warns readers not to confuse the two, calling the Chinatown one a bar-hopping street and the Sukhumvit one 'seedy'.

geography.notes: Only the Sukhumvit one is inside the unit; Chinatown Soi Nana is outside (citywide disambiguation)

claims.text_en: BTS Nana (E3) opened 5 December 1999 on the Sukhumvit Line, straddles the Khlong Toei and Watthana districts, is listed as one of the busiest BTS stations, and its entrances serve: Exit 1 the Soi 3/Soi 3/1 (Arab quarter) side with the Nana Nuea canal-boat pier, Exit 2 the Soi 4 side (Nana Plaza, Landmark Bangkok, Majestic Suites), Exit 3 the south side of Sukhumvit Rd, Exit 4 toward Soi 8; Wikipedia notes the station is 'surrounded by a variety of hotels and facilities for foreign tourists' and that Nana Plaza is within walking distance.

Exit 1: NH Bangkok Sukhumvit Boulevard (Soi 5, 200 m from station), Pakistan embassy, Nana Nuea pier (Soi 3, use Exit 1), eastbound bus stop; Exit 2: The Landmark Bangkok ('Skytrain station located in front of the hotel'), Majestic Suites, Nana Plaza (use Exit 2), westbound bus stop; Exit 3: Hyatt Regency/Ramada/Sofitel listings; Exit 4: ON8/lyf Sukhumvit 8; 'one of the busiest BTS stations in Bangkok'

claims.text_en: Nana Plaza, the adult-entertainment complex of roughly 24 go-go bars plus beer bars on three floors, sits at 3-4 Sukhumvit Soi 4 about 255-300 m from BTS Nana - inside the unit and roughly equidistant-or-closer than any rated neighbouring stop - and self-describes as 'the world's largest adult playground'. It grew from a late-1970s restaurant/shopping plaza, with go-go bars from the early 1980s (Wikipedia: opened 1983).

geography.notes: Wikipedia coordinates 13.74136, 100.55317 are ~255 m from the station anchor and ~490+ m from both rated neighbours st.phloen-chit and st.asok, so no clip ambiguity

evidence.paraphrase: Address 3-3/1 Sukhumvit Soi 4; about 300 m from BTS Nana; entertainment complex and red-light district; one of Bangkok's three concentrated red-light districts alongside Soi Cowboy and Patpong, all attracting primarily tourists; opened 1983, ~20 go-go bars by mid-1980s; U-shaped three-storey block around a courtyard

Operator: 'The Plaza now has 24 agogo bars and three stand-alone beer bars across three floors'; 39 venues existed by 2002; 'open 7 days a week 7 pm to 2 am'; recently celebrated two-millionth visitor

limitations: bar count conflicts: 24 (operator, current) vs 30 (Wikipedia, older data)

claims.text_en: Nana Plaza has undergone consolidation, not closure: bought in 2012 by Nana Partners Co Ltd (Fico Corporation and Panthera Group), renovated (about 10 M baht in lifts/escalators/electrical, an 18 M baht roof canopy in 2018, full CCTV), leasing to tenants on up to 12-year contracts, with the venue count falling from 39 bars (2002) to 24 agogo bars (operator's 2026 site) - bar churn with site-wide investment, consistent with reports of individual bar openings/closures in 2025 (Mandarin reopening Sep 2025, Orbit opening Nov 2025, Virgin closing) rather than any entertainment-zone shutdown.

temporal_scope.notes: 2025 bar-level events (Mandarin/Orbit/Virgin) rest on snippet-level search results only - recheck before publication

claims.text_en: Sukhumvit Soi 3/3/1 - 'Soi Arab' - is the Middle Eastern quarter of Bangkok inside this unit: the alley between Soi 3 and Soi 5, with Arabic signage, shisha/water-pipe cafes, Yemeni/Egyptian/Lebanese kitchens (Shahrazad opened 1983, Nasir al-Masri 1986), agarwood and perfume shops, and the nearby Grace Hotel described as popular among Arabs; the area serves Arab expatriates and visitors as a community and dining hub.

geography.notes: Wikipedia coordinates 13.7425, 100.5535 - north of Sukhumvit Rd, within ~350 m of the station anchor, well inside

temporal_scope.notes: Restaurant founding dates are from the Wikipedia article citing NYT 2008 / Reuters 2009

evidence.paraphrase: Soi Sukhumvit 3/1, also called Arab Street, between Soi Sukhumvit 3 and 5; mostly occupied by Middle Eastern visitors and expatriates; Shahrazad (1983) and Nasir al-Masri (1986); outdoor water-pipe smoking; agarwood shops; Grace Hotel not far away and popular among Arabs; foods from Lebanon, Iran, Yemen, India, Nepal, Thailand
Calls Soi 3/1 'Bangkok's Middle Eastern quarter' with shisha cafes, Yemeni grills and kitchens like Al Hussain; recommends spending an evening there
Odd-numbered side (Soi 3, Nana Tai) nicknamed Soi Arab for its Middle Eastern community - Arabic restaurants, kebab shops, travel agencies, tailors

claims.text_en: Rents in the unit's subdistrict (Khlong Toei Nuea) are consistent with the app's station-override estimate of 28,000 THB (1-bed) / 60,000 THB (2-bed) typical asking: PropertyScout shows 1-bed apartments averaging 37,429 THB (range 20,000-65,000) and 2-bed averaging 60,855 THB (range 32,000-88,570) across 88 listings (Nana clusters 15 of them); HipFlat's Nana-station page shows a 1-bed 62 sqm at 27,000 THB about 400 m from BTS Nana and 2-beds spanning roughly 32,000-84,000+ THB; a residential guide gives studios 12,000-20,000, 1-beds 'commonly 20,000-40,000', and larger 2-3BR/luxury units 60,000+. The app figures sit at the lower-middle of observed asking ranges and look like a reasonable 'typical' for ordinary stock, not for the luxury segment that dominates station-front towers.

claims.text_en: The main residential drawbacks reported for the unit are nightlife noise, cost-versus-space, and Sukhumvit traffic: a living guide says expect noise until very late near Soi 4/11, that 'you often pay more for less space than further-out Bangkok neighborhoods', that 'traffic on Sukhumvit can be heavy', and frames safety as 'more about being alert late at night than about crime - the area remains generally safe'; it recommends the area for convenience-seeking expats and against it for light sleepers, budget renters wanting more space, or car-dependent residents.

evidence.paraphrase: Noise near Soi 4/11 'until very late'; 'pay more for less space'; 'traffic on Sukhumvit can be heavy'; 'More about being alert late at night than about crime - the area remains generally safe'; suits expats/remote workers wanting centrality; less ideal for those seeking peace near Soi 4/11 or budget renters

limitations: single-source perceptions (corroborated in part by ThaiHometown's day/night contrast)

claims.text_en: A scam/tout environment is repeatedly reported around the unit's nightlife: community and guide sources describe padded or inflated bar bills in Nana Plaza venues (one 2026 Reddit report of a 2nd-floor go-go bar charging about 3x for two drinks; a TripAdvisor reviewer reporting a ~10,000 THB tab at Red Dragon), bar fines reported rising to about 1,000-1,500 THB in 2026, aggressive street touts on the Soi 4/Sukhumvit frontage steering visitors into venues, and drink-spiking warnings - with the same sources calling Nana Plaza safer than Patpong and advising bill-checking rather than avoidance.

claims.text_en: The 'Nana' identity straddles three registers that guides mix up: (1) the BTS-station catchment (this unit, spanning Sukhumvit Soi 1-9 frontage and the Soi 3/4 depth, split Watthana 48% / Khlong Toei 44% / Pathum Wan 8% per app data); (2) 'Soi Nana' specifically = Sukhumvit Soi 4 with the Nana Plaza complex, where Wikipedia's own district attribution ('Khlong Toei District') conflicts with the app's Watthana-majority split; and (3) the wider 'Nana intersection' usage on Sukhumvit Road. Sources in this batch use all three senses, often without saying which.

geography.place_name: Nana (BTS E3 / Soi Nana / Nana intersection)
geography.notes: Register confusion directly affects which venues are attributed to the unit

evidence.paraphrase: Station located on Sukhumvit Road 'at Soi Sukhumvit 9, east of Nana intersection (Soi Sukhumvit 3)' - using both the intersection and soi registers; straddles Khlong Toei and Watthana

Soi Nana named for the Lek-Nana family; BTS Nana station called the landmark serving the area

limitations: Wikipedia's 'at Soi Sukhumvit 9' station siting conflicts with the exits serving Soi 3/4 frontage; platforms likely span Soi 4-9 - unresolved

question_answers.notes: Aliases: BTS Nana / Nana intersection / Soi Nana (Soi 4) / Soi Arab (Soi 3/1). Straddles Khlong Toei + Watthana (station) with app split 48/44/8 incl. Pathum Wan sliver. Inside: Nana Plaza (~255-300 m), Soi Arab, Landmark (Exit 2 frontage), Bumrungrad (est.), Foodland block (snippet). Outside/boundary: Benchasiri (st.phrom-phong, ~1.2 km E), Lumphini Park (mostly st.lumphini, NE edge boundary), Nai Lert garden (Pathum Wan), Washington Square (unknown/not sourced, st.phrom-phong direction), Soi 9-13 cluster (st.asok side, partial), Soi 1 (st.phloen-chit, partial). Chinatown Soi Nana is a different street (c02).

Whose experience: Arab-community residents/visitors using Soi 3/1 kitchens and shisha into the small hours; bar-strip workers and tourists from 19:00-02:00(+); office/errand users on Sukhumvit frontage by day when the soi reads as a 'quiet business lane'; 24h Foodland users late at night (snippet).

What is valued: centrality and transit (busiest-station framing, one-stop Asok interchange), food diversity (Arab quarter's community function, 'home away from home' per Bangkok Post-era coverage), walkable daily support incl. Bumrungrad, and the nightlife/entertainment magnet itself. Mechanisms: station-front density + hotel stock + community specialization.

Counter-evidence: noise until late near Soi 4/11, pay-more-for-less-space, heavy Sukhumvit traffic, alertness-at-night framing; scam/tout environment around Nana Plaza (padded bills, rising bar fines, street touts) reported at snippet level with body-read counterweights. Sidewalk condition addressed via c13 (program improvements).

Day: business/residential lane, hospital and office traffic. Evening: Arab-quarter kitchens peak, bars from 19:00, plaza closes 02:00-03:00 (sources conflict). Weekday/weekend differentiation not documented in body-read sources. High-season tourist surge: not_found - no source read documents it.

Exits: E1 Soi 3 side (+ Nana Nuea pier), E2 Soi 4 side, E3 south side, E4 Soi 8 (editorial mapping, not official BTS). Sukhumvit skywalk runs along the corridor toward Phloen Chit per search-level info (not body-read) - flagged. BMA sidewalk program names Sukhumvit. No radius-to-time conversions used; junction-crossing conditions at Nana intersection not directly sourced.

Groceries: Villa Market walking distance (body-read), Foodland Soi 5 24h (snippet). Ordinary food: Arab-quarter kitchens, street frontage; tourist food: hotel/rooftop scene. Healthcare: Bumrungrad straddles the unit's NW edge (frontage ~415-450 m inside; geotagged center ~710 m outside the polygon). Gyms: Watchara Muay Thai Soi 1 (body-read listing); no chain-gym or pricing evidence.

Housing: older walk-up apartments + condos + serviced stock; asking rents 1-bed 20,000-65,000 (avg 37,429), 2-bed 32,000-88,570 (avg 60,855) in the subdistrict; station-adjacent examples (27,000 1-bed 400 m out) bracket the app's 28,000/60,000. App override is plausible for ordinary stock; sample = asking rents, portals, luxury-skewed, no signed-rent data.

Mapped 1.4 ha: UNIDENTIFIED (tools failed). Benchasiri 4.7 ha: outside (st.phrom-phong). Lumphini 57.6 ha: outside (~1.6-1.7 km to nearest edge, polygon-verified 2026-11-07). No walkable park documented in-unit; a guide reaches for Benjakitti 'a short ride away'. Green 10 is not reproducible from in-unit geometry on current evidence - the score needs surfacing/re-basing, e.g. on station-area proximity rather than catchment-interior green.

Fits: centrality-dependent workers/remote workers, long-stay expats wanting transit + food diversity + hospital access, Arab-community visitors, nightlife workers/visitors. Poor fit: light sleepers on Soi 4 frontage, families wanting green-and-quiet, budget renters wanting space, car users, scam-averse first-time tourists.

2024-2026: BMA sidewalk program incl. Sukhumvit (announced 2025-08-28, program 2024-2025); 'Sukhumvit model' cleaning plan Nana-Asoke-Phrom Phong (July 2025, snippet); Nana Plaza consolidation with 2018 roof canopy and 2012 takeover (dated), bar churn 2025 (Mandarin reopen 2025-09-21, Orbit open Nov 2025, Virgin close - snippet-level); residential guide published 2025-11-07 describing current conditions. No hotel openings/closures with dates, no BTS works specific to Nana found.

Contradictions: (1) nightlife 10 vs residential experience - 151 venues vs noise complaints and 'quiet by day' framing; (2) green 10 vs 1.4 ha mapped - unresolved, parks that would justify it are outside the clip; (3) safety 6 - consistent with 'alert at night' framing plus documented scam reports in a tourist-facing red-light zone, but no crime statistics found; (4) bar-count and closing-hour conflicts between operator and Wikipedia; (5) district attribution conflicts (plaza 'Khlong Toei' vs app Watthana-majority).

preview.text_en: A station-front hotel-and-entertainment quarter on lower Sukhumvit: the Soi 4 bar strip and Nana Plaza on one side, the Soi 3/1 Arab quarter's shisha cafes and late kitchens on the other, Bumrungrad hospital up the soi, and almost no mapped green inside the clipped catchment.

guide_lead.text_en: Nana (BTS E3, opened 1999) is the name for a stretch of lower Sukhumvit between roughly Soi 1 and Soi 9 whose odd and even sides 'are like two different worlds': to the north, Soi Nana (Soi 4) carries the bar strip and the three-floor Nana Plaza complex of about two dozen go-go bars, while Soi 3/3/1 - 'Soi Arab' - has anchored a Middle Eastern community of restaurants and shisha cafes since Shahrazad opened in 1983. Daytime it reads as a business-and-hotel lane; the same blocks run late. Daily-life support is unusually strong for a nightlife district: a 24-hour supermarket block at Soi 5 (snippet-level), Villa Market walking distance, and Bumrungrad hospital 350-500 m up Soi 3 with its own shuttle. Rents in the surrounding subdistrict average 37,429 THB for 1-bed and 60,855 THB for 2-bed asking, bracketing the app's 28,000/60,000 estimate. What the unit lacks is quiet and green: the nearest big parks - Benchasiri at Phrom Phong and Lumphini across Rama IV - sit outside the clipped catchment, and only 1.4 ha of park is mapped inside.

strengths.text_en: Transit centrality: E3 on the Sukhumvit Line, described as one of the busiest BTS stations, with three exits covering the Soi 3 (Arab quarter + pier), Soi 4 (bar strip) and south-side frontage
Two distinct food communities within 300 m of the exits: the Soi 3/1 Arab quarter (Yemeni, Egyptian, Lebanese kitchens since 1983-86) and the Sukhumvit frontage's tourist-and-hotel dining
Healthcare at the doorstep: Bumrungrad at 33 Soi Nana Nuea with a free shuttle from BTS Nana - a rare in-catchment amenity
24-hour service economy including the Soi 5 Foodland block (snippet-level) and late-night Arab-quarter kitchens that 'run past midnight'
Consistent rent reality: independent portal data brackets the app's 28,000/60,000 asking estimate, with ordinary 1-bed stock found at 27,000 THB ~400 m from the station

tradeoffs.text_en: Nightlife is the load-bearing feature and the main cost: noise 'until very late' near Soi 4 (and Soi 11, though that block sits on the st.asok side of the clip)
A scam/tout environment is repeatedly reported around the plaza and Soi 4 frontage - padded bills, touts, spiking warnings - even though the same sources call it 'generally safe' beyond that

Green inside the clipped unit is minimal: 1.4 ha mapped on 0.97 sq km, with Benchasiri outside at Phrom Phong and Lumphini's nearest edge a ~0.7-0.8 km boundary case requiring an arterial-road crossing
Space-per-baht is poor: 'you often pay more for less space than further-out Bangkok neighborhoods', and Sukhumvit traffic is heavy for car users
Identity confusion is real editorial work: three registers of 'Nana' (station area / Soi 4 / intersection) plus the separate Chinatown Soi Nana mean guides attribute venues to the wrong unit

day_night.text_en: Day: 'fairly quiet business/residential lane' on Soi Nana itself; hospital, office and errand traffic on the Sukhumvit frontage; hotel breakfast-and-tour circuit
Evening: Arab-quarter kitchens peak ('come hungry, come late', Al Hussain runs past midnight) while the bar strip and Nana Plaza light up from 19:00
Late night: plaza closes 02:00-03:00 (operator vs Wikipedia conflict); the 24-hour Foodland block and late shisha cafes take over the residual demand

within_area_variation.text_en: Odd/even split: Soi 3/3/1 Arab community quarter vs Soi 4/5 hotel-bar strip - 'like two completely different worlds'
Soi-by-soi noise gradient: frontage and Soi 4 loud until late; deeper residential pockets 'quieter by day'; guide names Soi 10/12 as quieter but that sits beyond the east clip

West/east clip asymmetry: the Soi 9-13 hotel cluster (Marriott, Hyatt Regency Sukhumvit, Sofitel/Ramada) falls outside or borderline into st.asok's catchment, though station guides list it under Nana exits
South-of-Sukhumvit even-soi blocks are the residential face, with their far southern depth clipped off by st.lumphini's catchment

conditional_fit.text_en: Good fit: long-stay expats and remote workers who want centrality, transit, food diversity and hospital access and can accept noise - 'single professionals, couples, and even families who want central access' per the residential guide
Good fit: Arab-community and Muslim travellers using the Soi 3/1 quarter's kitchens, groceries and halal infrastructure
Poor fit: light sleepers or families prioritizing green and quiet - the nearest major parks are outside the clipped unit
Poor fit: budget renters wanting space and car-dependent residents - higher cost per sqm and heavy Sukhumvit traffic
Poor fit (situational): first-time tourists averse to touts and bill-padding around the plaza; the same area is rated 'generally safe' for alert residents

uncertainties: The mapped 1.4 ha park could not be identified (Overpass/Nominatim failed) - green 10's basis is unresolved and probably rests on station-area proximity to parks outside the clip [nana-c14]
Clip geometry rests on Wikipedia infobox coordinates with a suspected error for BTS Asok; east/west clip soi boundaries carry ~1-2-soi uncertainty until GIS-verified [nana-c15]

Scam specifics (padded-bill incidents, 2026 bar-fine levels) are snippet-level because TripAdvisor and Reddit fetches returned 403; only the general tout/price environment is body-read supported [nana-c12]
Bar count (24 vs 30) and closing hour (02:00 vs 03:00) conflict between the operator's site and Wikipedia [nana-c04]
High-season tourist surges and weekday/weekend rhythm differences: not found in body-read sources [Q05]
Nana Plaza's district attribution ('Khlong Toei' per Wikipedia) conflicts with the app's Watthana-majority split for Soi 4 [nana-c18]
